title: Regulatory Fragmentation, Consumer Acceptance and Capacity Constraints in Lab-Grown Food: Evidence from 2026 Disclosures

detail.title: Regulatory Fragmentation, Consumer Acceptance and Capacity Constraints in Lab-Grown Food: Evidence from 2026 Disclosures

detail.abstract: This paper examines the commercial and regulatory conditions facing lab-grown food, defined here as cultivated animal-cell products and food ingredients made by precision fermentation, using evidence published in 2026 only. The analysis rests on an evidence base of fourteen sources: legislative texts, a national food regulator's consumer survey, price statistics, company reports and regulatory announcements, and financial-press coverage of beef prices. Every figure was logged when read and traced to its source, and derived measures are labeled as the authors' calculations. The findings point to a split between regulatory clearance and legal access to buyers. Approvals in Singapore continued to accumulate, while United States state legislatures and courts moved toward moratoria and labeling rules, and European authorities indicated that assessment capacity is still being built. Survey data from the United Kingdom show that opposition to sale (43 percent) exceeds support (35 percent), and that safety and naturalness concerns outweigh price concerns. Disclosed fermentation capacity is far larger than any disclosed cultivated-cell capacity, which suggests that fermentation-derived ingredients are likelier to reach industrial buyers first. Record beef prices narrow the price gap with conventional meat but do not, on the evidence reviewed, change stated willingness to eat. A listed investor in the sector trades at a steep discount to reported asset value, which indicates tight capital-raising conditions. The paper closes with implications for procurement heads, supply chain and strategy leads, investors and policymakers, and with a statement of the limits of a single-year evidence window.

title: Preemptive Enterprise Resilience Through Cascading-Impact Modeling and Resource-Constrained Recovery Prioritization

detail.title: Preemptive Enterprise Resilience Through Cascading-Impact Modeling and Resource-Constrained Recovery Prioritization

detail.abstract: Financial service organizations depend on interconnected business processes, digital systems, communication channels, and workforce resources, making localized disruptions capable of propagating across multiple functions. This study develops a preemptive enterprise resilience framework to identify dependency bottlenecks, quantify cascading business impacts, and prioritize mitigation actions under limited resources. Business processes are modeled as nodes in a directed, weighted, multilayer dependency network. AHP and TOPSIS are combined to prioritize vulnerable processes using business criticality, dependency centrality, service impact, recovery duration, redundancy deficiency, resource intensity, and disruption exposure. A threshold based cascade model then evaluates disruption propagation, affected processes, cascade depth, service degradation, and Business Impact Score. Candidate interventions are tested through cascade re simulation, and a resource constrained 0 1 integer optimization model selects feasible mitigation portfolios. Using a synthetic financial service network of 60 processes and controlled disruption scenarios, the dependency bottleneck scenario affected 19 processes and produced a Business Impact Score of 0.76. The selected mitigation portfolio reduced affected processes to 7 and the Business Impact Score to 0.24, representing a simulated 68.4% reduction in business impact. The findings show how dependency based prioritization and resource constrained mitigation can support preemptive resilience planning.

detail.abstract: In defining the relationship between resource and performance heterogeneity among firms, the existing resource-based view (RBV) literature overlooks the inherent lifespans of strategic resources. The strategic resource decay (SRD) framework (Karadag and Poppo, 2023) challenges one of the main tenets of the RBV regarding the sustainability of resource-driven competitive advantage by exploring how strategic resources decay—endogenously lose their value-creating potentials. This paper empirically examines and extends the SRD framework. Using panel data of 631,491 firm-month observations from 2,696 upstream operators, this study finds evidence that, regardless of its predictable and endogenous nature, the depletion of firm reserves in the Permian Basin, currently the largest oil-producing area in the US, negatively affects the subsequent—nationwide—oil production of these firms. Further, all else constant, the capability reconfiguration activity of the firms often does not suffice to retain production levels. This paper also extends the SRD framework by introducing a new boundary condition—scarcity—and finds evidence that the extent of scarcity of a given type of strategic resource intensifies the negative impact of its decay on firm performance. These results validate SRD as an internal source of dynamism that potentially threatens firm performance through the depletion of strategic resources, calling for further investigation and the integration of the concept of SRD in resource-based research. This study provides both an initial empirical examination of SRD and guidance for future empirical research on this topic.

detail.abstract: Early detection of cardiovascular disease is critical for timely clinical intervention. Leveraging the increasing availability of ElectronicHealth Records (EHRs) and physiological signals, recent advances in deep learning have shown promise in predictive modeling;however, existing approaches often struggle to jointly capture structural feature interdependencies and long-range temporaltrends inherent in heterogeneous clinical data modalities. This study evaluates an adaptive attention-based deep learning architecturethat integrates Graph Attention Networks (GAT) with Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) networks, augmentedby a temporal attention mechanism, to optimize predictive performance without early feature fusion. The framework is evaluatedacross two distinct clinical objectives: binary cardiovascular risk prediction using the cross-sectional Framingham Heart Studydataset, and multi-class diagnostic superclass classification using the high-resolution PTB-XL ECG dataset, with a derived binaryNORM vs. Non-NORM screening view for clinical triage evaluation. Class imbalance within the Framingham training folds isaddressed using the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), applied strictly within each training fold to preventdata leakage. On the Framingham dataset, 5-fold stratified cross-validation yields an accuracy of 88.73 ± 1.54%, an AUC-ROCof 94.57 ± 0.67%, and an F1-score of 0.90. On the held-out PTB-XL test split, the model achieves a NORM-screening accuracyof 96.20%, a precision of 0.85, a recall of 0.98, and an F1-score of 0.91 with an overall 5-class classification accuracy of 96%.These outcomes outperform competitive machine learning and deep learning baselines, verifying the framework’s adaptability andcapability to process heterogeneous clinical modalities.

detail.abstract: (Objective) Posterior systolic curling (PSC) is a dynamic mechanical abnormality of the posterior mitral annulus and adjacent inferobasal left ventricular wall associated with ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death, yet its assessment remains qualitative and lacks standardized quantitative criteria. We developed an automated echocardiographic framework that learns regional spatiotemporal signatures of posterior annular–myocardial hypermobility from parasternal long-axis cine-loops and selectively integrates the most informative temporal windows for patient-level PSC detection.(Methods) A retrospective cohort of 100 subjects (40 PSC, 60 noPSC; 44 women; median age 58 years) was analyzed, with PSC status assigned by three blinded clinicians. A segmentation network localized the posterior annulus–ventricular wall complex, and regional motion was encoded using TV-L1 optical flow. A CNN–Transformer was pretrained through contrastive learning, masked motion modeling, and temporal ordering, and patient-level classification was performed using Top-K multiple instance learning. Performance was evaluated using nested stratified patient-level cross-validation, component-wise ablation experiments, and temporal relevance analysis.(Results) The framework achieved a mean AUC of 0.910, accuracy of 0.86, sensitivity of 0.83, specificity of 0.88, and F1-score of 0.83. Removing self-supervised pretraining, replacing optical flow with raw images, or using mean pooling reduced performance. The complete three-task pretraining objective outperformed partial task combinations, supporting complementary learning signals. Model relevance was concentrated predominantly in pre-end-systolic and intermediate-to-late systolic windows.(Conclusion) Self-supervised regional motion learning combined with weakly supervised temporal aggregation demonstrated the feasibility of automated patient-level PSC detection from standard echocardiographic cine-loops and may support more reproducible assessment of this dynamic phenotype.

detail.abstract: Water infrastructure can generate agricultural gains while changing the climate costs of production. We examine this trade-off using China's South-North Water Diversion Project (SNWDP) and a staggered difference-indifferences design. Water delivery increases county-level agricultural methane (CH4) emissions by approximately 81 tons annually and induces adjustments toward rice-based cultivation. Valuing the dynamic emissions response under four alternative methane valuation scenarios, we estimate that climate damages offset 2.52-6.61% of the project's estimated agricultural benefits. The effect operates primarily through a shift toward water-intensive rice cultivation and is larger in counties with effective land titling at the onset of water delivery, consistent with tenure security facilitating costly crop conversion. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating non-CO2 greenhouse gas impacts into the evaluation of agricultural development policies.

title: Revenue Sharing as Extra Competition: Why n Siblings Bid Like n + 1 Strangers

detail.title: Revenue Sharing as Extra Competition: Why n Siblings Bid Like n + 1 Strangers

detail.abstract: When partners auction a jointly owned asset among themselves, each bidder receives part of the price even when she loses. With independent private values and constant absolute risk aversion (CARA), such revenue sharing affects bids exactly as additional competition does, extending a risk-neutral observation of Lengwiler and Wolfstetter (2005). If each of n bidders receives a fraction s of the price, the bids when the price is the winning bid are those of a standard first-price auction against (n-1)/(1s) rivals; when the price is the second-highest bid, they are those of a seller in a first-price procurement auction against 1/s rival sellers. With equal shares both numbers equal n, so an n-partner dissolution auction produces the bids of a first-price auction with n + 1 bidders, or of a procurement auction with n + 1 sellers. The equivalence holds for every value distribution only under CARA or linear utility. Under decreasing absolute risk aversion, revenue sharing moves bids by less than one extra bidder would; under increasing absolute risk aversion, by more. For every utility, bidding one's value guarantees each partner the value of her share.
